label: Encoding phase: original-token inputs and the <DEL> step
explanation: Broad phase feature: fires on nearly every step of the original-token phase (~93% of steps, independent of token identity) and on the <DEL> delimiter step (96%), and is essentially silent throughout the copy phase (0.3% of copy steps, ~0 mass). Magnitude is tiny at t=0 (about 1% of mass despite 87% firing), rises over the first few positions, and the largest activations are at <DEL> in short sequences (top examples are L=3 with <DEL> at ~6.9). Not selective for token identity, digits vs letters, or repeats (in_first correlation is just a side effect of the phase split).

issues: None of the checks found a real problem. On the test split, 'phase < 2' gives precision 0.938, recall 0.998, F1 0.967 and mass recall 0.9996, matching the reported scores.

Phase claims hold on the dev profile: the feature fires on 93.4% of original-phase steps, 96.3% of <DEL> steps and 0.3% of copy steps (0.000 of activation mass). t=0 fires 86.7% of the time but carries only 1.2% of mass, and the top 12 examples are all L=3 sequences peaking at <DEL> at about 6.9.

Token claims hold: precision stays between 0.92 and 0.96 within the encoding phase for digits, repeated tokens (in_count>=2) and in_first==0. Firing rate is flat (about 0.52-0.54) across token identities.
Missed activations (8124 test steps) carry 0.0% of mass; they are faint traces (about 0.01-0.07 of max) early in the copy phase.

False positives (230k steps, about 6%) are scattered. They are somewhat concentrated at t<=1 (precision 0.86) and at <DEL> for L=9 (precision 0.89), where the activation decays and some sequences go silent for a run of late original tokens. Precision in both places stays well above 0.5, so carving them out would lower F1. This is noise, not a systematic counterexample class.
Minor: 'grows over the first few positions' holds for magnitude (t=0 is near zero), but the firing rate at t=0-1 (about 0.86) is already close to later steps (0.95-0.98).
